name: Gatecraft
author: Gatecraft

sections.description:
The tour shows every edition. Some features need Gatecraft Pro.

Gatecraft turns a WordPress site into a box office for the events you run. Ticket pages live at one address on your site (default: /events/) and use your theme’s header and footer. Everything else is managed under the “Gatecraft” menu in wp-admin.

  • Events and venues, with ticket categories that each have a price and a capacity (for example Gold 5,000, Silver 2,500, Standard 1,500).
  • Overselling is prevented with database row locks, also when many people buy at once.
  • Card payments with Stripe Checkout, and offline payments you define yourself (bank transfer, PayPay, cash and so on) with your own instructions. Choose which methods each event allows. Offline bookings wait as “Payment to confirm” until you confirm the payment, then the buyer receives their tickets.
  • Local payment methods through Stripe next to cards: iDEAL, Bancontact, EPS, Przelewy24, BLIK, TWINT and SEPA Direct Debit in Europe, konbini and PayPay in Japan, and Cash App Pay, Amazon Pay, Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay and ACH bank debit in the US.
  • PayPal, and Razorpay for events in India (UPI, cards including RuPay, netbanking and wallets). Refunds from the booking page, a tax rate and name, and the currency you sell in.
  • A time zone per event, for events in another country or online. Dates, times and prices follow each visitor’s language.
  • Add to calendar and Google Calendar buttons on the event page, the booking page and the ticket email, and a calendar feed of your public events that calendar apps can subscribe to.
  • Optional agreement to your terms at checkout, policy pages, and a business details page for the Japanese Specified Commercial Transactions notice.
  • Discount codes, limited by event, ticket category, dates, number of uses and minimum tickets.
  • Emails with QR code tickets and a calendar invite. Edit every email’s wording. An email log shows what was sent, and failed emails are retried.
  • A printable ticket sheet with an organiser note and a larger QR code, which buyers can save as a PDF.
  • Your logo, brand colour and button style. Ticket pages use your theme’s header and footer.
  • Links in the footer of your ticket pages: Instagram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn and your website with their own icons, and up to 8 other links with a general icon.
  • Free bookings confirmed by email before tickets are issued, so bots cannot claim every free place.
  • Duplicate an event to a new date, or cancel an event in one step with an optional email to the buyers.
  • Repeating events: create many dates at once (daily, weekly on chosen days, monthly on a date or a weekday such as the second Friday, or a list of dates), with dates to skip. Each date is its own event, and changes can be applied to the others. Event pages let visitors pick a date.
  • High-demand protection: a quick person check at checkout (Cloudflare Turnstile) for events where bots would otherwise take the tickets.
  • A month calendar of your events, as a layout of the events list, the shortcode, the Elementor widget and the Gatecraft events block for the block editor.
  • Blocks for the block editor: Gatecraft events, Gatecraft event (a whole event page with its ticket form) and Gatecraft ticket button. Pick the event from a list.
  • Share buttons on public event pages: LINE, WhatsApp, Facebook, X, email and copy link. Plain links: nothing loads from those sites until a visitor taps one.
  • An alert to your team, in the admin and by email, when an event nears selling out.
  • Import events, venues and tickets from The Events Calendar and Events Manager, as drafts to check and publish.
  • The living gate on event pages: a gate of dots that fills in as tickets sell. Status wording such as Sold out and Few left, and link previews with the event image.
  • Consent to hear from you collected at checkout, and an Audience list to view who agreed, with the wording and date.
  • Ticket pages, emails, tickets and the admin in English and Japanese, and in every language translated on translate.wordpress.org or added with a plugin such as Loco Translate. A language switcher for visitors, buyers and staff, a language per event, and emails in each buyer’s language.
  • Door scanner that runs in a phone’s browser, with duplicate and wrong-event detection.
  • A dashboard with revenue, upcoming events and a daily sales chart, sales reports, and CSV exports of bookings and attendees.
  • Staff roles for managers and door staff, two-step sign-in for staff with a trusted browser option, login lockout and an audit log. Uploaded images are re-encoded and strict security headers are sent.
  • Confirm it’s you: before risky changes, such as giving someone staff access, changing payment details or sign-in settings, or downloading many people’s details, staff enter their password (and authenticator code) again, at most once every 15 minutes.
  • Security alerts by email to every Gatecraft admin straight away: new WordPress administrators or ticketing managers, payment details or sign-in settings changed, authenticators removed and many failed staff sign-ins. Staff also get an email when their account signs in from a browser it has not used before.
  • An optional check that refuses passwords found in known data breaches (off until you switch it on).
  • Security check: every Gatecraft program file is compared once an hour with the file list of the release (and, if you switch it on, with the checksums WordPress.org publishes). Changed, missing or unexpected files, including program files in the Gatecraft uploads folder, are reported to every admin at once.
  • Personal data export and erase through WordPress’s privacy tools.

Gatecraft Pro

An optional paid add-on for organisers who need more. It adds Sign in with Google, Audience tools (filters, saved lists, tags, export), emails to your audience, the visual page designer, invoices (including Japanese qualified invoices), high-demand protection against ticket bots, imports from other ticketing platforms, approval before payment, automatic and group discounts, checkout questions, event reminders, waiting lists, repeating events, wallet passes, Google Sheets sync, Excel exports and extra reports. Everything listed above stays free and works without it.

External services

Gatecraft works without any external service. These connections are used only if you set them up:

Stripe (card payments)

Used when you set up Stripe and turn on card payments. When you set it up, the key is checked with Stripe, Gatecraft creates its webhook in your Stripe account and reads which payment methods are switched on there. When a buyer chooses to pay by card, the plugin sends the booking reference, ticket names, quantities, prices, currency and the buyer’s email address to Stripe to create a Checkout session, and receives payment confirmations from Stripe’s webhook. Refunds you start from the booking page are also sent to Stripe.
Stripe Services Agreement: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa
Stripe Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

PayPal (payments)

Used when you set up PayPal and turn on PayPal. When you set it up, the keys are checked with PayPal and Gatecraft creates its webhook in your PayPal app. When a buyer chooses PayPal, the plugin sends PayPal the booking’s total, currency, booking number, event title and the addresses to return to, and the buyer pays on PayPal’s page. Gatecraft then asks PayPal to take the payment and checks it, receives payment updates from PayPal’s webhook (each one checked with PayPal), and sends refunds you start from the booking page. The buyer’s details on PayPal are handled by PayPal.
PayPal User Agreement: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/useragreement-full
PayPal Privacy Statement: https://www.paypal.com/myaccount/privacy/privacyhub

Razorpay (payments in India)

Used when you set up Razorpay and turn it on, for events priced in Indian rupees. When you set it up, the keys are checked with Razorpay. When a buyer chooses Razorpay, the plugin sends Razorpay the booking’s total, the currency, the booking number, the event title, the buyer’s name and email address and the address to return to, and the buyer pays on Razorpay’s page. Gatecraft then reads the payment link from Razorpay to check the payment, receives payment updates from Razorpay’s webhook, and sends refunds you start from the booking page.
Razorpay Terms of Use: https://razorpay.com/terms/
Razorpay Privacy Policy: https://razorpay.com/privacy/

Google Calendar (calendar links)

The Google Calendar buttons are plain links. Nothing is sent until a visitor clicks one: their browser then opens calendar.google.com with the event’s title, times, address and page link filled in.
Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Pwned Passwords (breached password check)

Used only when an admin switches on “Refuse passwords found in data breaches” under Gatecraft > Settings > Sign-in and security. When someone sets a new password on the site, the plugin sends the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash to api.pwnedpasswords.com and checks the answer on your server. The password itself, and the rest of its hash, never leave the site. Nothing else is sent.
Have I Been Pwned API terms: https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3
Have I Been Pwned Privacy Policy: https://haveibeenpwned.com/Privacy

Cloudflare Turnstile (high-demand protection)

Used only when you set up Turnstile and switch on “High-demand protection” for an event. On that event’s page the Turnstile script is loaded from challenges.cloudflare.com and checks that the buyer is a person. When the buyer books, Gatecraft sends the Turnstile answer and the buyer’s IP address to Cloudflare to verify it. No other data is sent.
Cloudflare Website and Online Services Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
Cloudflare Turnstile Privacy Addendum: https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/
Cloudflare Privacy Policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

WordPress.org checksums (Security check)

Used only when an admin switches on “Compare program files with WordPress.org” under Gatecraft > Settings > Sign-in and security. The Security check then downloads the published file checksums of the installed Gatecraft version from downloads.wordpress.org, once per version. The request sends only the version number (and your site’s usual request details such as its IP address).
WordPress.org Privacy Policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

YouTube and Vimeo (videos in event descriptions)

Used only when you paste a YouTube or Vimeo link into an event description. The video is shown in an embedded player, which the visitor’s browser loads from YouTube (www.youtube-nocookie.com) or Vimeo (player.vimeo.com) when they open the event page. The plugin itself sends nothing to these services; the visitor’s browser sends its usual request (IP address, browser details) to load the player.
YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
Vimeo Terms of Service: https://vimeo.com/terms
Vimeo Privacy Policy: https://vimeo.com/privacy

Source code and libraries

All code and the stylesheet are human-readable and unminified. There is no build step.

  • php-qrcode by chillerlan (MIT): https://github.com/chillerlan/php-qrcode
  • php-settings-container by chillerlan (MIT): https://github.com/chillerlan/php-settings-container
  • jsQR by Cosmo Wolfe (Apache 2.0), used by the door scanner: https://github.com/cozmo/jsQR
  • Inter font by Rasmus Andersson (SIL Open Font License 1.1): https://github.com/rsms/inter

Privacy

The plugin stores bookings, buyer names, email addresses, optional phone numbers and checkout answers in your WordPress database. They are included in Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data. Staff sign-ins, payments confirmed and settings changes are recorded in an audit log. For staff accounts, a cookie (gatecraft_dev) and a list of up to 20 browsers the account has used are kept, to send the new-browser notice.
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip, and activate.
  2. Go to Gatecraft > Settings: set your brand, the ticket page address, currency and payment methods. Set the currency before the first booking; it locks once bookings exist.
  3. Permalinks must not be set to “Plain” (Settings > Permalinks).

  4. Optional services: set up Stripe, PayPal, Razorpay and Cloudflare Turnstile under Gatecraft > Settings > Integrations. Follow the steps and paste your keys; Gatecraft checks them with the service, stores them encrypted and makes the Stripe and PayPal webhooks itself. Changing keys that are in use takes effect after a day, and every admin is told. You can put the keys in wp-config.php instead, which always wins:

    define(‘GATECRAFT_STRIPE_SECRET’, ‘sk_live_…’);
    define(‘GATECRAFT_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET’, ‘whsec_…’);

    define(‘GATECRAFT_INTEGRATIONS_IN_CONFIG_ONLY’, true); switches setting up in the admin off. The Integrations page lists every constant.

Background work (emails and expiring unpaid holds) runs every minute through WP-Cron. On a live site, run it from a real cron job:

define('DISABLE_WP_CRON', true);
* * * * * cd /path/to/site && wp gatecraft worker --quiet

Requires the PHP extensions sodium, gd, mbstring and openssl. The plugin shows a notice if one is missing. The intl extension is recommended: with it, dates and prices follow each visitor’s language beyond English and Japanese.
sections.faq:
Can buyers pay in cash or with PayPay?

Yes. Add the method under Gatecraft > Settings > Checkout and payments with your instructions. The buyer sees them after booking and by email. You confirm the payment on the booking page, which sends the QR tickets.

How do I add tickets to a normal page?

Use the shortcodes:

[gatecraft_events limit="6" category="Music"]   Grid of upcoming public events. Add view="small", "medium", "wide", "full" or "list" to change the layout.
[gatecraft_button event="event-address" label="Get tickets"]   Button to one event's ticket page.
[gatecraft_event slug="event-address"]   The whole event page with booking, inside any page.

With Elementor, drag the Gatecraft event, Gatecraft events or Gatecraft ticket button widget from the Gatecraft group in the Elementor panel and pick the event from a list. No shortcode to type.

Can I use Gatecraft in my language?

Yes. Gatecraft uses standard WordPress translations. Japanese ships with the plugin; other languages come from translate.wordpress.org, or you can make your own with a plugin such as Loco Translate. Switch each language on under Gatecraft > Settings > Regional. With no default chosen, visitors see the site’s WordPress language when Gatecraft has it.

Does it work with my theme?

Ticket pages are wrapped in your theme’s header and footer. Each release is tested with the most used themes: Twenty Twenty-Five, Twenty Twenty-Four, Hello Elementor, Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Blocksy and Neve, on desktop and phone. Styles are scoped so they do not change the rest of your site.

What are the WP-CLI commands?

wp gatecraft worker Run the background work now.
wp gatecraft reset-2fa Clear a staff member’s authenticator.
wp gatecraft unlock Clear sign-in lockouts.

2026.1.0.0

The first public release. Versions are numbered YEAR.RELEASE.FEATURE.PATCH from here on.

  • Events, ticket categories with early-bird prices, venues with sections, and capacity for the event, each category and the venue.
  • Event pages you design on the page itself, with colours, fonts, banner shapes and full-width layouts, for the whole site or one event.
  • The living gate: the Gatecraft gate fills in as tickets sell, and the red dot appears in the doorway when the doors open.
  • Booking with built-in spam protection, discount codes, an optional limit per booking, guest lists and door sales.
  • Card payments, konbini and PayPay through Stripe; bank transfer, PayPay, cash and your own methods, with payment details per event and a queue to confirm them.
  • Tax included or added, and invoices with sequential numbers and the Japanese registration number.
  • QR tickets by email, a print-ready ticket sheet, calendar invites and email text you can edit.
  • A check-in scanner in the browser on any phone or tablet, and a door staff role.
  • An audience list with news and notices, and import of contacts and past bookings from Peatix, Eventbrite, Ticket Tailor, LivePocket, TIGET or any CSV file.
  • A dashboard, reports, CSV exports, notifications, a daily summary, email and audit logs, and a quick finder (Ctrl+K).
  • Staff roles, two-step sign-in, personal data export and erasure, and English and Japanese throughout.
  • “Match my theme”, the [gatecraft_event] shortcode (works on Elementor pages) and a description editor with the Media Library.
  • The Gatecraft brand in the admin and About Gatecraft. Your own logo and colours on the ticket pages, emails and tickets, and an optional “Powered by Gatecraft” line, off unless you turn it on.
  • Gatecraft Pro adds approval before payment, checkout questions, automatic and group discounts, a waiting list, repeating events, Apple and Google Wallet passes, reminders and messages to ticket holders, Excel exports, more reports and Google Sheets sync.

  • Import events, venues and tickets from The Events Calendar and Events Manager, as drafts to check and publish.
  • The living gate on event pages: a gate of dots that fills in as tickets sell. Status wording such as Sold out and Few left, and link previews with the event image.
  • Consent to hear from you collected at checkout, and an Audience list to view who agreed, with the wording and date.
  • Ticket pages, emails, tickets and the admin in English and Japanese, and in every language translated on translate.wordpress.org or added with a plugin such as Loco Translate. A language switcher for visitors, buyers and staff, a language per event, and emails in each buyer’s language.
  • Door scanner that runs in a phone’s browser, with duplicate and wrong-event detection.
  • A dashboard with revenue, upcoming events and a daily sales chart, sales reports, and CSV exports of bookings and attendees.
  • Staff roles for managers and door staff, two-step sign-in for staff with a trusted browser option, login lockout and an audit log. Uploaded images are re-encoded and strict security headers are sent.
  • Confirm it’s you: before risky changes, such as giving someone staff access, changing payment details or sign-in settings, or downloading many people’s details, staff enter their password (and authenticator code) again, at most once every 15 minutes.
  • Security alerts by email to every Gatecraft admin straight away: new WordPress administrators or ticketing managers, payment details or sign-in settings changed, authenticators removed and many failed staff sign-ins. Staff also get an email when their account signs in from a browser it has not used before.
  • An optional check that refuses passwords found in known data breaches (off until you switch it on).
  • Security check: every Gatecraft program file is compared once an hour with the file list of the release (and, if you switch it on, with the checksums WordPress.org publishes). Changed, missing or unexpected files, including program files in the Gatecraft uploads folder, are reported to every admin at once.
  • Personal data export and erase through WordPress’s privacy tools.

Gatecraft Pro

An optional paid add-on for organisers who need more. It adds Sign in with Google, Audience tools (filters, saved lists, tags, export), emails to your audience, the visual page designer, invoices (including Japanese qualified invoices), high-demand protection against ticket bots, imports from other ticketing platforms, approval before payment, automatic and group discounts, checkout questions, event reminders, waiting lists, repeating events, wallet passes, Google Sheets sync, Excel exports and extra reports. Everything listed above stays free and works without it.

External services

Gatecraft works without any external service. These connections are used only if you set them up:

Stripe (card payments)

Used when you set up Stripe and turn on card payments. When you set it up, the key is checked with Stripe, Gatecraft creates its webhook in your Stripe account and reads which payment methods are switched on there. When a buyer chooses to pay by card, the plugin sends the booking reference, ticket names, quantities, prices, currency and the buyer’s email address to Stripe to create a Checkout session, and receives payment confirmations from Stripe’s webhook. Refunds you start from the booking page are also sent to Stripe.
Stripe Services Agreement: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa
Stripe Privacy Policy: https://stripe.com/privacy

PayPal (payments)

Used when you set up PayPal and turn on PayPal. When you set it up, the keys are checked with PayPal and Gatecraft creates its webhook in your PayPal app. When a buyer chooses PayPal, the plugin sends PayPal the booking’s total, currency, booking number, event title and the addresses to return to, and the buyer pays on PayPal’s page. Gatecraft then asks PayPal to take the payment and checks it, receives payment updates from PayPal’s webhook (each one checked with PayPal), and sends refunds you start from the booking page. The buyer’s details on PayPal are handled by PayPal.
PayPal User Agreement: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub/useragreement-full
PayPal Privacy Statement: https://www.paypal.com/myaccount/privacy/privacyhub

Razorpay (payments in India)

Used when you set up Razorpay and turn it on, for events priced in Indian rupees. When you set it up, the keys are checked with Razorpay. When a buyer chooses Razorpay, the plugin sends Razorpay the booking’s total, the currency, the booking number, the event title, the buyer’s name and email address and the address to return to, and the buyer pays on Razorpay’s page. Gatecraft then reads the payment link from Razorpay to check the payment, receives payment updates from Razorpay’s webhook, and sends refunds you start from the booking page.
Razorpay Terms of Use: https://razorpay.com/terms/
Razorpay Privacy Policy: https://razorpay.com/privacy/

Google Calendar (calendar links)

The Google Calendar buttons are plain links. Nothing is sent until a visitor clicks one: their browser then opens calendar.google.com with the event’s title, times, address and page link filled in.
Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Pwned Passwords (breached password check)

Used only when an admin switches on “Refuse passwords found in data breaches” under Gatecraft > Settings > Sign-in and security. When someone sets a new password on the site, the plugin sends the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash to api.pwnedpasswords.com and checks the answer on your server. The password itself, and the rest of its hash, never leave the site. Nothing else is sent.
Have I Been Pwned API terms: https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3
Have I Been Pwned Privacy Policy: https://haveibeenpwned.com/Privacy

Cloudflare Turnstile (high-demand protection)

Used only when you set up Turnstile and switch on “High-demand protection” for an event. On that event’s page the Turnstile script is loaded from challenges.cloudflare.com and checks that the buyer is a person. When the buyer books, Gatecraft sends the Turnstile answer and the buyer’s IP address to Cloudflare to verify it. No other data is sent.
Cloudflare Website and Online Services Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
Cloudflare Turnstile Privacy Addendum: https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/
Cloudflare Privacy Policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

WordPress.org checksums (Security check)

Used only when an admin switches on “Compare program files with WordPress.org” under Gatecraft > Settings > Sign-in and security. The Security check then downloads the published file checksums of the installed Gatecraft version from downloads.wordpress.org, once per version. The request sends only the version number (and your site’s usual request details such as its IP address).
WordPress.org Privacy Policy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

YouTube and Vimeo (videos in event descriptions)

Used only when you paste a YouTube or Vimeo link into an event description. The video is shown in an embedded player, which the visitor’s browser loads from YouTube (www.youtube-nocookie.com) or Vimeo (player.vimeo.com) when they open the event page. The plugin itself sends nothing to these services; the visitor’s browser sends its usual request (IP address, browser details) to load the player.
YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
Vimeo Terms of Service: https://vimeo.com/terms
Vimeo Privacy Policy: https://vimeo.com/privacy

Source code and libraries

All code and the stylesheet are human-readable and unminified. There is no build step.

  • php-qrcode by chillerlan (MIT): https://github.com/chillerlan/php-qrcode
  • php-settings-container by chillerlan (MIT): https://github.com/chillerlan/php-settings-container
  • jsQR by Cosmo Wolfe (Apache 2.0), used by the door scanner: https://github.com/cozmo/jsQR
  • Inter font by Rasmus Andersson (SIL Open Font License 1.1): https://github.com/rsms/inter

Privacy

The plugin stores bookings, buyer names, email addresses, optional phone numbers and checkout answers in your WordPress database. They are included in Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data. Staff sign-ins, payments confirmed and settings changes are recorded in an audit log. For staff accounts, a cookie (gatecraft_dev) and a list of up to 20 browsers the account has used are kept, to send the new-browser notice.
